1.explanation: Prism’s core configuration is in components.js under the “languages” object—there is no entry for PlantUML (or .wsd/.puml), so Prism never highlights it. Moreover, gulpfile.js/paths.js defines which language component files are bundled when building; without adding the new prism-plantuml.js path here, even if the language file exists it won’t be included in the final distribution. Editing components.js to register PlantUML and updating paths.js to include its component file are the key steps to enable PlantUML support.
1.bug_scenario: The user is writing PlantUML diagrams (in a .wsd file) and previewing them side-by-side in VSCode. While the diagram renders correctly, there is no syntax highlighting for the PlantUML source because Prism doesn’t know about the PlantUML language. The screenshot shows unhighlighted text on the left and a rendered UML diagram on the right.

2.explanation: Prism’s language registry is driven by the `components.js` file, which enumerates every supported language under its `languages` object. Since PlantUML isn’t listed there, Prism never attempts to load a corresponding definition. In addition, the build configuration in `gulpfile.js/paths.js` (specifically its `main` array) only bundles the core and a fixed set of languages and plugins; it must be updated to include `components/prism-plantuml.js` (or whichever file implements the PlantUML grammar). Updating these two files is therefore essential to register, build, and ship the new PlantUML language support.
2.bug_scenario: When editing a `.wsd` PlantUML file in VSCode with the Prism-based PlantUML preview plugin, no syntax highlighting rules or language definition are applied. In the screenshot on the left you can see a valid PlantUML text file, but on the right the rendered preview is unstyled and the PlantUML keywords aren’t recognized. This indicates that Prism isn’t loading a PlantUML language component.
